title: REMOVE_SESSION_NAME special transaction audit
scope: Pinned OpenHarmony communication_ipc source commit bbb92dbb2f52aca54ab268307c9476ac1802f3ff; bounded to REMOVE_SESSION_NAME receive/send chain, guards, permission effect, and existing tests.

verdict.reason: The handler removes a SoftBus permission for a caller-supplied nonempty session name, but its special transaction code is rejected by the ordinary IPCObjectProxy::SendRequest path. The internal bypass is used by IPCProcessSkeleton cleanup against the registry/SAMgr proxy. Handler additionally requires a local Binder caller and the receiving process's SAMgr registry flag. No untrusted route to the bypass was found in the reviewed scope. Exact product build pairing remains unverified.

pinned_source_binding.binding_note: Matches the previously independently recorded pinned source SHA for ipc_object_stub.cpp; this file-level binding is stronger than the checkout HEAD mismatch.

unverified_binding: The local full checkout is not at the requested commit.
The matching file-level SHA for ipc_object_stub.cpp does not establish that every send-side/helper/test file is byte-identical to the requested commit.
No product build manifest / resolved dependency graph pairing the requested commit with its deployed binaries was available in this audit.

evidence.claim: REMOVE_SESSION_NAME dispatches to DBinderRemoveSessionName from IPCObjectStub::SendRequest under CONFIG_IPC_SINGLE exclusion.
evidence.detail: The special code case calls DBinderRemoveSessionName(code, data, reply, option); the dispatch is compiled only when CONFIG_IPC_SINGLE is not defined.

evidence.claim: The receive handler requires both a local Binder call and the receiver process SAMgr flag.
evidence.detail: It rejects if !IPCSkeleton::IsLocalCalling() || !IsSamgrCall(). IsSamgrCall reads ProcessSkeleton::GetInstance()->GetSamgrFlag(); the flag is set true after successful IPCProcessSkeleton::SetRegistryObject.

evidence.claim: The guarded operation reads one string and removes the matching permission entry.
evidence.detail: ReadString result is rejected only when empty. DBinderSoftbusClient::DBinderRemovePermission decrements the locally tracked session-name reference count and invokes the dynamically resolved SoftBus removal function when the count reaches zero. No ownership check or session-name syntax/UID-PID validation occurs in this handler.

evidence.claim: The public proxy SendRequest rejects the special transaction code before forwarding.
evidence.detail: Any code > MAX_TRANSACTION_ID is rejected except DUMP_TRANSACTION. REMOVE_SESSION_NAME is a special code above MAX_TRANSACTION_ID in the protocol constants.

evidence.claim: The internal sender is IPCProcessSkeleton cleanup using the SAMgr proxy.
evidence.location: IPCProcessSkeleton::RemoveSessionName, approximately lines 1340-1355; IPCObjectProxy::RemoveSessionName, approximately lines 359-371
evidence.detail: IPCProcessSkeleton obtains GetSAMgrObject(), invokes IPCObjectProxy::RemoveSessionName(sessionName); that helper writes the session string and calls SendRequestInner(false, REMOVE_SESSION_NAME, ...) with TF_ASYNC, bypassing the public code-range validation. This is an internal lifecycle route, not the public SendRequest route.

evidence.claim: IsLocalCalling describes transport locality rather than caller authorization; in this path the additional SAMgr flag is receiver-process state.
evidence.detail: DBinderDatabusInvoker::IsLocalCalling returns false. IPCProcessSkeleton sets the flag on successful registry-object registration; IsSamgrCall reads that process-global flag. These guards block remote DBinder arrival and constrain handling to a receiving process marked as SAMgr, but IsSamgrCall alone does not identify the caller.

normal_internal_flow: It gets the SAMgr/registry object and invokes IPCObjectProxy::RemoveSessionName.
The helper serializes the session string and uses internal SendRequestInner with REMOVE_SESSION_NAME.
IPCObjectStub::SendRequest dispatches the special code to DBinderRemoveSessionName.
Receiver checks IsLocalCalling and receiver-side GetSamgrFlag before reading the string and decrementing/removing the permission.
untrusted_public_flow_checked: A caller using IPCObjectProxy::SendRequest with REMOVE_SESSION_NAME fails the code > MAX_TRANSACTION_ID guard before transport.
A remote DBinder databus request fails IsLocalCalling.

attacker_capability_assessment.ordinary_local_app_via_public_proxy_api: No reachable path found; special transaction is rejected in public SendRequest.
attacker_capability_assessment.caller_with_internal_proxy_helper_or_cus: Not established. Would need access to private/internal SendRequestInner path, a custom invoker, modified IPC exports, or an in-process route capable of issuing the special code. If such access exists, the handler has no name ownership check and can decrement an arbitrary name's tracked permission count; impact depends on matching name/refcount and receiver identity.

existing_unit_coverage: test/unittest/ipc/native/core/ipc_object_stub_unittest.cpp: DBinderRemoveSessionNameTest003 checks successful guarded removal with a mocked SoftBus callback.
coverage_gaps: No reviewed end-to-end test verifies that public SendRequest rejects REMOVE_SESSION_NAME while the internal lifecycle helper succeeds.
No reviewed test checks whether a SAMgr receiver rejects a forged local special transaction from an ordinary local process when injected below the public proxy guard.
No reviewed test checks cross-UID/session-name ownership semantics; current code only rejects an empty string.

counterevidence: Public proxy API enforces the special transaction code boundary.
The sole located production callsite is lifecycle cleanup on IPCProcessSkeleton's SAMgr proxy.
The SAMgr flag is established when registry object registration succeeds, rather than from data supplied in the transaction.
next_steps: Bind ipc_object_proxy.cpp and ipc_process_skeleton.cpp from the exact requested commit and confirm their symbol visibility/export status, since local checkout HEAD differs.

If target build exposes an internal raw transaction path to untrusted local code, add a focused test that attempts REMOVE_SESSION_NAME for a different UID/PID session and verifies permission/refcount isolation.
Otherwise retain 0 candidate and record the target-product build provenance gap; do not promote the missing ownership check by itself.
limitations: No tests were run, as instructed.
Source review does not establish deployed binary reachability or the exact c_utils/SoftBus versions paired with the requested IPC commit.
